text.p: The Turkish lira eased to 91,770 against the dollar on Monday in thin trade from 91,400 at Friday's close on the central bank's higher dollar rate for banks' forex transfers, bankers said.

The Turkish central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers at 91,600 lira at the opening, versus 91,400 at Friday's close. It further raised the rate to 91,750 lira in the afternoon.
Bankers said cash demand remained strong as banks repaid the central bank a total of 45.9 trillion lira borrowed overnight at 75 percent on Friday and at previous repo auctions.

The central bank injected a total of 73.1 trillion lira -- 20.4 trillion lira by buying ten-day repos at an average annual rate of 74.67 percent in an open market auction and 52.7 trillion lira by overnight lending at 75 percent interbank.
Overnight money also traded at 74.75 percent in the day.
T-bill yields firmed by around one point ahead of the treasury's announcement of this week's t-bill auction on cash shortage.
The average yield on the most heavily traded April 9 paper firmed to 128.55 percent from 127.95 on Friday.
The second most active March 26 paper yielded 128.12 percent, up from 127.48 percent Friday average.
The treasury will auction 217-day t-bills on Tuesday with Wednesday value date when 93.1 trillion lira will be cashed in from maturing t-bills. -- Istanbul Newsroom, +90-212-275 0875
